module.title: Giving Lifestyle Advice: Should, Shouldn't & Ought To
module.group: A2.2 - Social Dynamics, Work & Everyday Life
module.objective: Offer lifestyle, health, and study advice using modal verbs 'should', 'shouldn't', and 'ought to'.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Healthy Lifestyle Choices
subModules.grammarFocus: Modals of advice: should, shouldn't, and ought to

content.summary: Welcome to the reading mission on giving lifestyle advice. In this unit, you will read about daily habits, health tips, and how to use should, shouldn't, and ought to to give good advice to friends and family.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Using should, shouldn't, and ought to for advice and recommendations.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words related to daily routines, health, stress, and habits.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skimming for general ideas and scanning for specific health recommendations in short texts.

learningObjectives: Understand the main ideas of short A2 texts about healthy habits and routines.
Locate specific lifestyle advice details in written passages.
Recognize and apply grammar patterns with should, shouldn't, and ought to.

contextWarmup.prompt: When your friend feels tired all day, what is the best advice to give them?
options: You should sleep earlier and drink more water.
You ought to eat fast food every night.
You shouldn't rest at all.
contextWarmup.explanation: Sleeping earlier and drinking water are healthy habits that help cure tiredness.

rules: Should + verb without 'to': Use this to give positive advice or recommendations. Example: You should drink more water.
Shouldn't + verb without 'to': Use this to give negative advice or light warnings. Example: You shouldn't eat too much sugar.
Ought to + verb: This has the same meaning as should but sounds a bit more formal. Example: You ought to get enough sleep.

commonTrap.explanation: Learners often put the word 'to' after should, but modal verbs are followed directly by the base verb without 'to'.
commonTrap.wrong: You should to exercise every day.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Patterns with Should and Ought To
grammarFormulas.description: Assemble sentence blocks to practice advice structures:

items.exampleSentence: You should change your lifestyle to be healthier.
Can you give me some advice about healthy eating?
You ought to exercise regularly, at least three times a week.
You should eat a balanced diet with vegetables and protein.
You shouldn't worry too much because stress is bad for your health.
You should avoid junk food if you want to lose weight.
You ought to improve your sleeping habits.
You should develop good habits like drinking water every morning.
You shouldn't drink so much coffee. You should reduce your caffeine intake.
You ought to have a morning routine to start your day well.

paragraphs: Are you feeling tired all the time? Do you want to feel better and have more energy for school and sports? You ought to look at your daily lifestyle and make some positive changes. Many teenagers have bad habits like sleeping late and eating junk food every day. However, small changes can make a big difference in your health.

First, you should eat a balanced diet with plenty of fresh vegetables, fruit, and water. You shouldn't drink too much soda or coffee because they are bad for your sleep. Second, you should exercise regularly. You can play football, ride a bike, or walk to school. Finally, you ought to reduce stress by relaxing and sleeping eight hours every night. A good morning routine helps you start the day with a smile.

options: Small lifestyle changes can improve your health and energy.
Teenagers should never rest or relax.

content.summary: Focus on listening for specific suggestions and recommendations using modal verbs. Notice how speakers emphasize should and ought to when giving advice in everyday conversations.
learningObjectives: Catch the main topic of a spoken conversation about daily habits.
Identify details such as advice and recommendations using modal verbs.
Notice how words link together in connected speech during fast conversations.

keyPhrases.note: Used to describe chronic fatigue or lack of daily energy.
Common habit of missing the first meal of the day.
Remaining awake past normal bedtime to watch shows or work.
Taking time to relax or sleep to recover physical energy.

connectedSpeech.note: The word should often reduces to a weak form /ʃəd/ in fast speech.
The preposition to in ought to reduces to /tə/.
Pronoun I links smoothly after should.
A linking sound /j/ is inserted between stay and up.

content.summary: Practical guide on sentence structure and paragraph building in English for giving healthy lifestyle advice using modal verbs.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Positive Advice with Should
blueprintItems.example: You should drink more water every day.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Negative Advice with Shouldn't
blueprintItems.example: You shouldn't eat too much sugar at night.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Formal Advice with Ought To
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + ought to + base verb + complement
blueprintItems.example: We ought to get enough sleep before work.

mechanicsRules.rule: Modal verbs like should and ought to are followed by the base form of the verb without 'to'.
mechanicsRules.badExample: You should to exercise every morning.
mechanicsRules.why: Modal verbs take bare infinitives directly.

mechanicsRules.rule: Do not use auxiliary verbs like 'do' or 'does' with modals when forming negative advice.
mechanicsRules.badExample: You don't should stay up late.
mechanicsRules.why: Modals act as their own auxiliaries in negative forms.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always capitalize the first word of a sentence and place a full stop at the end.
mechanicsRules.badExample: we should eat more fresh vegetables.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: We should eat more fresh vegetables.
mechanicsRules.why: Standard English sentence punctuation rules apply to all advice sentences.

practicumQuestions.promptText: You should eat fast food every single day.
targetAnswers: You shouldn't eat fast food every single day.
practicumQuestions.explanation: To give negative lifestyle advice, use 'shouldn't' followed by the base verb 'eat'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using 'ought to' instead of 'should':
targetAnswers: We ought to protect our environment.
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Ought to' has the same meaning as 'should' but is slightly more formal.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the capitalization and punctuation in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.hint: Capitalize the first letter and keep the full stop.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Every sentence in English must begin with a capital letter.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the advice sentence with the correct modal verb for positive advice:
practicumQuestions.promptText: You ___ sleep for eight hours every night to stay healthy.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the modal verb for positive recommendation.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Both 'should' and 'ought to' can express positive recommendations.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Turn this statement into a question asking for advice:
practicumQuestions.hint: Put 'Should' at the beginning of the sentence and add a question mark.
practicumQuestions.explanation: To ask for advice, place the modal verb 'Should' before the subject 'I'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix the verb form error after the modal verb in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.hint: Remove the 's' from the main verb.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Modal verbs must always be followed by the base form of the verb without adding 's' or 'es'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two advice sentences using 'because':
practicumQuestions.promptText: You should wear a jacket. It is cold outside.
practicumQuestions.hint: Join the sentences with 'because' in the middle.
targetAnswers: You should wear a jacket because it is cold outside.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use 'because' to explain the reason behind the advice.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences using 'so':
practicumQuestions.promptText: She exercises every morning. She stays very healthy.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'so' to show the result of the action.
targetAnswers: She exercises every morning so she stays very healthy.
She exercises every morning, so she stays very healthy.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use 'so' to connect an action to its positive result.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change this negative advice into positive advice:
practicumQuestions.promptText: You shouldn't stay up late on weekdays.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change 'shouldn't' to 'should' and adjust the verb if necessary (e.g., sleep early).
targetAnswers: You should sleep early on weekdays.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Replacing 'shouldn't' with 'should' requires an opposite positive action such as sleeping early.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a complete sentence giving advice to someone who has a headache:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Write advice for a headache using 'should'.
practicumQuestions.hint: Example: You should rest in a quiet room.
targetAnswers: You should rest in a quiet room.
practicumQuestions.explanation: A correct advice sentence starts with a subject, uses 'should', and ends with a base verb phrase and a full stop.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Giving Lifestyle Advice with Should and Ought To

content.summary: In this speaking lab, you will learn how to give lifestyle advice clearly using modal verbs such as should, shouldn't, and ought to. Focus on clear vowel sounds, sentence stress on key advice words, and friendly intonation when talking about health habits.
content.audioGuidance: Listen carefully to how modal verbs are often unstressed in fast speech, while main verbs and advice nouns carry the main sentence stress. Keep your tone encouraging and polite.

pillars.name: Modal Reduction
pillars.explanation: In fast spoken English, should often sounds like /ʃəd/ and shouldn't sounds like /ˈʃʊdnt/ with a quick final /t/.

pillars.name: Sentence Stress
pillars.explanation: Stress words like advice, lifestyle, balanced, and reduce to make your suggestions sound clear and helpful.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice how the primary stress shifts when changing from the noun to the related adjective.
The stress moves to the fourth syllable in the noun form.
The stress moves to the second syllable in the continuous form.
The stress shifts to the second syllable in both words, but the vowel changes slightly.

drills.targetText: You should eat a balanced diet every single day.
drills.phonetic: /juː ʃʊd iːt ə ˈbælənst ˈdaɪət ˈevri ˈsɪŋɡl deɪ/
drills.focus: Modal verb should with clean vowel sounds
drills.hint: Keep should short and stress balanced and diet.

drills.targetText: You ought to exercise regularly to improve your health.
drills.phonetic: /juː ˈɔːt tuː ˈeksəsaɪz ˈreɡjʊləli tuː ɪmˈpruːv jɔː helθ/
drills.focus: Using ought to smoothly in advice
drills.hint: Link ought to together as ought-ta.

drills.targetText: You shouldn't stress too much about small problems.
drills.phonetic: /juː ˈʃʊdnt stres tuː mʌtʃ əˈbaʊt smɔːl ˈprɒbləmz/
drills.hint: Pronounce the quick final t in shouldn't clearly.

drills.targetText: You should reduce your coffee intake to sleep better.
drills.phonetic: /juː ʃʊd rɪˈdʒuːs jɔː ˈkɒfi ˈɪnteɪk tuː sliːp ˈbetə/

practicumQuestions.instruction: Use falling intonation at the end of giving advice statements.

practicumQuestions.targetSentence: You should eat a balanced diet.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Lower your pitch at the end of the sentence to sound confident and reassuring.
